## Reasons for Previous UI

Women gave an average of 2.7 specific reasons for having UI in the past 3 months. Women who had fewer than three acts of UI gave an average of 1.9 reasons; women who had more UI gave an average of 3.0 reasons (p 05; data not shown) The most common groups of reasons for having had UI in the 3 months before conception were that did not think were going to get pregnant ( 42%), had trouble getting a contraceptive method ( 40%), and weren't planning on having sex (38%) (Table 2). The most common specific reason was, "Idid not think I was going to have sex (34%), followed by thinking one could not become pregnant because of one's place in the menstrual out of birth control   supplies (20%) and the partner not wanting to use birth control (19%) What they they they they cycle distinguished women who had frequent UI (three or more times in the 3-month period ) from women with few reported acts was greater reporting of access problems (inability to afford, diffi culty getting to the clinic, and not wanting to see doctor), history of side effects from contraception; partner who did not want to use birth control, and higher level of ambivalence about becoming pregnant.

## Attitudes Toward UI

The most prevalent attitude about UI was that it "feels better Or more natural, an opinion held by 48% of respondents. Just over one third (36%) said it was to have once in a while or at certain times of the month" (Table 3). One in four women relationship reasons to UI were significantly associated with a willingness to have UI in the future.
